title: Azure Databricks: workspaces, clusters and Unity Catalog

videos.script: Lesson 20 wrote Quitanda's night as code. Somewhere has to run it, every night, on Spark. Azure Databricks is the most common answer. {{answer}} A Databricks workspace is split in two. Databricks runs the control plane. The clusters run in your subscription, or in Databricks' serverless plane. {{planes}} You will declare a workspace inside Quitanda's own network, with no public addresses, and check it with Terraform on your laptop. {{declare}} Then the compute. A cluster people share, a cluster that lives for one job, a SQL warehouse, and serverless. {{compute}} The bill is DBUs, plus the machines underneath. The same half hour of work can cost four and a half times as much, or seventy times, depending on which you chose. {{bill}} And Unity Catalog. Every table gets a three-part name, and every grant names one. The lake is reached through an identity, never a key. {{catalog}} Nothing in Databricks has an emulator, so most of this lesson comes from the documentation, and says so. {{docs}}
